title: daisugi
text: daisugi experimental machine learning package focused unconventional tree systems, probabilistic boosting, interpretable ensembles, emerging recursive partitioning methods. workflows daisugi follow simple pattern: “grow_*()” fits machine “harvest_*()” generates predictions package primarily uses explicit “(x, y)” interfaces classification regression tasks.

title: daisugi
text: typical daisugi workflow: prepare predictors targets grow machine harvest predictions evaluate externally using preferred tooling daisugi intentionally avoids imposing modeling framework instead focuses exposing novel algorithms lightweight interface.

title: daisugi
text: showcasing use daisugi classification. dataset comes forested, tabular data repo lists forest attributes & whether area “forested” “non-forested”.

title: daisugi
code: library(daisugi) library(forested) library(rsample) set.seed(5311)  # defining splits for training and testing datasets splits <- rsample::initial_split(forested::forested) training <- rsample::training(splits) testing <- rsample::testing(splits)   # (x, y) Training: x_train <- training |>   # target (and factors as not all engines handle cats)   dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)  # our target variable: y_train <- training |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()  # (x, y) Testing: x_test <- testing |>   dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)  y_test <- testing |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()  head(y_test) #> [1] No  Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes #> Levels: Yes No

title: daisugi
text: Yggdrasil Decision Forests (YDF) Google’s high-performance tree ecosystem supporting gradient boosted trees, random forests, specialized split strategies. implementation exposed daisugi emphasizes: oblique random splits scalable forest construction modern decision forest infrastructure
code: ydf_trees <- grow_yggdrasil_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 5L ) #> Downloading uv...Done! #> Train model on 5330 examples #> Model trained in 0:00:00.038857  harvest_yggdrasil_trees(ydf_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes"

title: daisugi
text: SnapBoost originates IBM’s Snap ML ecosystem. Unlike traditional gradient boosting systems, SnapBoost uses heterogeneous Newton boosting iteration may alternate : decision trees linear regressors random Fourier feature approximators creates hybrid ensemble structure rather purely tree-based booster.
code: snap_trees <- grow_snap_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 5L )  harvest_snap_trees(snap_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "No" "No" "No" "No" "No" "No"

title: daisugi
text: Perpetual budget-driven boosting methodology designed around adaptive predictive scaling rather extensive hyperparameter tuning. core idea : increase predictive budget monitor loss stabilization stop improvement plateaus creates AutoML-like boosting workflow minimal tuning overhead.
code: perpetual_trees <- grow_perpetual_trees(   x_train,   y_train )  harvest_perpetual_trees(perpetual_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] 0 0 0 0 0 0

title: daisugi
text: WildWood advanced probabilistic random forest algorithm emphasizing aggregation multiple possible tree prunings. Unlike standard random forests, WildWood combines: randomized forests exponential weighting --bag pruning aggregation produces highly adaptive ensemble behavior.
code: wild_trees <- grow_wild_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 5L )  harvest_wild_trees(wild_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "No"  "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes"

title: daisugi
text: Explainable Boosting Machines (EBMs) interpretable generalized additive boosting systems developed Microsoft’s InterpretML project. EBMs aim balance: predictive performance transparency interaction discovery human interpretability often considered “glassbox” models learned structure remains directly inspectable.
code: explainable_trees <- grow_explainable_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 5L )  harvest_explainable_trees(wild_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] "Yes" "No"  "Yes" "Yes" "Yes" "Yes"

title: daisugi
text: NGBoost introduces probabilistic prediction gradient boosting systems. Rather predicting point estimates, NGBoost models predictive distributions directly using natural gradients. enables: uncertainty estimation probabilistic forecasting calibrated predictive intervals
code: natural_trees <- grow_natural_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 5L ) #> [iter 0] loss=0.6879 val_loss=0.0000 scale=4.0000 norm=8.0000  harvest_natural_trees(natural_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] 0 0 0 0 0 0

title: daisugi
text: NRGBoost energy-based generative boosting algorithm. design require target(y) variable logic added daisugi ease--use.
code: energy_trees <- grow_energy_trees(   x_train,   y_train |> as.integer() - 1,   trees = 5L )  harvest_energy_trees(energy_trees, x_test) |> head() #> [1] 0.07347243 0.45393993 0.07087025 0.45357028 0.19876139 0.18953708  # fun fact: NRG can draw samples: energy_trees$fit$sample(5L)

title: daisugi
text: Evolutionary Trees comes {evtree} R package. involves evolutionary learning global optimal trees classification regression.
code: evolutionary_trees <- grow_evolutionary_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 10L )  harvest_evolutionary_trees(evolutionary_trees, x_test) |> head() #>   1   2   3   4   5   6  #> Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes  #> Levels: Yes No

title: daisugi
text: Conditional Trees (conditional forest) ported {partykit::cforest} implementation. cforest bagging algorithm ctree p-value tree-based algorithm.
code: conditional_trees <- grow_conditional_trees(   x_train,   y_train,   trees = 10L )  harvest_conditional_trees(conditional_trees, x_test) |> head() #>   1   2   3   4   5   6  #> Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes  #> Levels: Yes No
